## Fixes

**Signalith Agent**
- Fluent Bit's buffer on each computer is capped at 1 GB (4 GB on a network sensor). While Signalith cannot be reached the oldest events are dropped past that, rather than filling the computer's disk. Agents pick this up by themselves; a Fluent Bit you set up by hand gets it when you download its configuration again from **Add data**. (ASI-01)
- When Signalith refuses a computer's token three times in a row, the agent stops Fluent Bit and osquery instead of reading events Signalith would drop, and starts them again from where they were once the token is accepted. (ASI-01)
- An agent update now rolls back when the new version starts but cannot reach Signalith, not only when it fails to start. (ASI-04)

**Load balancers**
- The HAProxy and keepalived samples in `deploy/loadbalancer` now check `/readyz` for syslog too (over TLS, TCP and UDP), so a server that is starting, stopping, drained or cut off from OpenSearch gets no syslog from the balancer. Copy the new checks into a balancer set up from the old samples. See [Load balancers](https://signalith.io/docs/load-balancers/). (DEP-01)

## Security fixes

- **One account can no longer sign everyone else out.** Each user keeps at most 50 sign-in sessions; a 51st ends that user's oldest, never another user's. Before, enough sign-ins by one account on a single server pushed out the sessions of every other user, admins included.
- **Windows: Signalith's own account no longer has access to OpenSearch's folder.** `C:\ProgramData\SignalithOpenSearch`, which holds the CA key and the admin certificate, gave `NT SERVICE\Signalith` full control. It is now SYSTEM and Administrators only (OpenSearch's own account keeps its settings, data and logs). Running the 0.3.2 installer fixes an existing install.
- **The NVD API key stays on its server.** It no longer follows a redirect to another server, and the NVD, KEV and EPSS downloads now go through the same checks as threat intel feeds, so they never reach this machine, Signalith's OpenSearch or a cloud metadata service. An NVD mirror on this machine needs `intel.allow_loopback_feeds`, as feeds do.
- **Approving a server means typing its fingerprint.** The Servers page and `signalith cluster approve <name>` at a terminal ask for the fingerprint the new server shows on its sign-in page or in its log, instead of a checkbox or a yes next to the fingerprint OpenSearch holds, which anyone who can write to OpenSearch could have made. Lists of waiting servers show only the first group of each fingerprint.
- **The audit integrity check catches deleted audit indices.** With every audit index, or every record in them, deleted, **Check integrity** and `signalith audit verify` reported a clean result. They now report the records removed when servers sign their records, also when other records were put in their place.
